role: Senior Lecturer in Bioinformatics, University of Sheffield (bio); helping non-coding colleagues
workflow: migrating lab data out of Prism after institutional licence loss
quote: I'm trying to help people (with 0 coding experience or desire to gain coding experience) transition out of GraphPad PRISM as our uni has removed our license. Does anyone have any thoughts on the best way to get data out of Prism without a licence?
problem: University dropped the Prism licence; non-coders cannot open or move their own Prism data
need: Open and import Prism project files (.prism and .pzfx) without a Prism licence, for users who will not code

workflow: bulk recovery of years of Prism project files
quote: There appear to be both python and R parsers for the old .pzfx files, but not the new .prism ones. I'm talking about over a decade of work in some peoples cases - 100s of files.
problem: Hundreds of .prism files per person, a decade of work, with no parser for the new format
need: Batch-import a folder of .prism/.pzfx files and recover every data table with its labels

quote: What I've seen is that it's completely closed format intended to lock people into the product. ... Hopefully they'll change direction and realize that locking up people's data is just going to drive many people away to use R and Python only.
problem: Perceives the new Prism file format as a closed lock-in of users' own data
need: Save projects in a documented open format (e.g. zipped CSV + JSON with a published schema) so data stay readable without the vendor

quote: I feel like it wouldn't be that hard if I understood PRISM's data model. Like, what's the difference between a sheet and a table and a dataset?
problem: The Prism data model (sheet vs table vs dataset) is opaque even to a bioinformatician
need: Document the project data model (data tables, analyses, graphs) in plain terms and in the file schema

role: Professor of cell biology, University of Warwick (bio)
quote: I have only dealt with the .pzfx files in the past. It sounds like they've tightened up. Is it possible to get a trial version and automate export of data?
problem: Only workaround offered for locked files is a trial licence plus scripted export
need: Provide a free reader/exporter that batch-exports every table to CSV

quote: Please #Prism, I really need support for Linux, I can pay you money
problem: Prism has no Linux version; a paying user on Linux cannot run it
need: Run in any browser / on Linux with the same features as the desktop app

workflow: running Prism on Linux for work
quote: it is for my job, I ended up having to crack it and using wine but I kind of hate it
problem: Needed Prism for work on Linux; ended up with a cracked copy under Wine
need: A cross-platform tool that runs natively on Linux, so nobody has to crack or emulate it

workflow: choosing a test for lab results
quote: Diving deep into #Statistics, #R and #prism to try to figure out whether to use #ANOVA or #ttest to analyse our results. ... It can be a luxury as a busy PI
problem: A PI has to research for themselves whether to run ANOVA or t-tests
need: A design-first test chooser that asks how many groups and factors there are and explains why it picks ANOVA or a t-test

workflow: multi-omics analysis for a clinical PI
quote: we cannot change the statistical test just because you don't like the p-value
problem: PI wants to switch tests after seeing the p-value
need: Record the test chosen before results are shown and keep an audit trail of any later change

quote: multiple-testing correction needs to be done even though your favorite gene becomes insignificant.
problem: Pressure to skip multiple-testing correction when a favoured gene loses significance
need: Apply multiple-comparison correction by default and show corrected and uncorrected values together

quote: Sample size of N=3 when dealing with multi-omics is *too* small
problem: N=3 per group is used for multi-omics
need: Warn about low power for the planned N and offer a sample-size calculation before data collection

quote: I have rarely seen power calculation and Statistical Analysis Plan done prior to data collection in the university hospitals.
problem: Power calculations and analysis plans are rarely done before data collection
need: Offer a pre-registration style analysis plan and power calculation that the later analysis is checked against

role: Retired physicist, ML and stats for cancer drug discovery (bio)
workflow: gene-level testing in cancer drug discovery
quote: I've faced *exactly* that situation in the past. (Right down to "change the stat so the p-value is better", and "stop with the FDR correction because my favorite gene isn't high enough".)
problem: Pressure from scientists to swap tests and drop FDR correction
need: Make FDR correction and the chosen test visible, locked and logged so dropping them is an explicit, recorded act

quote: In my experience, the fix is usually to invest in making the N much larger (robots, high throughput, which then teaches people just how much noise they had in the first place) .
problem: Small-N biology underestimates noise until high-throughput replication reveals it
need: Show replicate-to-replicate and plate-to-plate variability so users see how noisy their assay is

quote: Anyone know of a good way to examine EDS files from a Thermofisher RT-PCR machine that doesn't require installing the software suite? ... But I fundamentally oppose data locked into a proprietary format for long-term archiving.
problem: qPCR instrument output (.eds) cannot be read without the vendor suite
need: Import instrument run files (e.g. Thermo .eds) directly and keep an open copy

workflow: qPCR analysis and plotting in R
quote: So, I'm thinking about good R packages to do analyses of #qPCR data. ... Something that gives some really nice and versatile plots or something that could pipe right into #ggplot is really desired.
problem: Has to evaluate several R packages to analyse and plot qPCR data
need: Built-in qPCR (ΔΔCt) analysis whose results flow straight into flexible plots

quote: Every few days I have the urge to contact authers to tell them, that their p-value being bigger than .05 does NOT mean that there is no effect.
problem: Authors read p > 0.05 as 'no effect'
need: Report effect sizes with confidence intervals next to p and word non-significant results as 'not detected', not 'no effect'

quote: It is frustrating to see how biologists, after having spent years with expensive experimental research, misinterpret their own work.
problem: Biologists misinterpret their own statistics after years of experiments
need: Plain-language interpretation of each result, with common misreadings flagged

role: Group leader, MRC LMB / Professor, Cambridge, neuroscience (bio)
quote: However, current estimation tools struggle with the complex, multi-group comparisons common in biological research. ... There's institutional-wide need for change in the biological sciences when it comes to statistical handling of data.
problem: Estimation (effect-size) tools do not handle shared-control, repeated-measures and two-way designs
need: Estimation graphics (mean differences with CIs) for shared-control, repeated-measures and two-way designs

role: Reader commenting on an immunology preprint (bio: news/books account)
quote: the use of six tumor growth plots with mismatched Y-axis scales weakens the data’s clarity and scientific integrity.
problem: Six tumour growth panels with different y-axis scales mislead comparison
need: Lock y-axes across panels of a figure by default and warn when panels that will be compared have different scales

quote: After students asked for one for years, I have now made a simple figure design checklist. To help all scientists w/o graphic design training create clearer, more accessible, and truthful charts!
problem: Students without design training have asked for years for guidance on figures
need: A built-in figure checklist that checks clarity, accessibility and honesty before export

quote: if your scales don't start at zero: indicate this clearly, not only in text but also visually (especially for bar charts etc)
problem: Bar charts with truncated axes are not marked visually
need: Force bar charts to start at zero, or draw a visible axis break when they do not

quote: don't just scale down the image (as a scaled down font is _not_ the same as a smaller font size). Oh, and (if the publication allows you to do this): use vector graphics (e.g. directly generated pdf), not bitmap.
problem: Figures get scaled down, so fonts shrink unevenly, and are exported as bitmaps
need: Set the final figure size and font size in points at export, and export vector PDF/SVG

role: Data visualisation specialist; Open Source in Pharma workshop (bio)
quote: Use {ggview} to preview plots at the same size and resolution as you want to save them with ggsave() to avoid the annoying resizing
problem: The on-screen plot differs from the saved file, so figures need repeated resizing
need: Show the figure at its true export size and DPI while editing (WYSIWYG export)

quote: We are working on a paper where we show that 29 % of papers in top journals like Science, Nature & PNAS were skewed by a single influential data point!
problem: A single influential point skews results in many published papers
need: Flag influential points (e.g. DFFITS/Cook's distance) on every fit and show the result with and without them

quote: Due to a recent discussion with colleagues on whether and when to use #LinearMixedModels (#LMM), I wrote a blog post comparing LMM to other approaches using simulated data.
problem: Lab colleagues are unsure when nested/hierarchical data need a mixed model
need: Detect nested designs (cells within animals) and offer a mixed model or aggregation, explaining the choice

workflow: tSNE/UMAP of flow and mass cytometry
quote: Ever use a #tSNE or #UMAP in #scSeq, #flowcytometry or #masscytometry? It doesn't have to be just a pretty picture anymore - we've developed a statistical test to check for differences.
problem: Group differences on tSNE/UMAP plots are judged by eye, with no test
need: Offer a statistical test for differences between groups in cytometry embeddings that respects biological replicates

quote: Although I grumble about the quality of #scientific #software (and there’s a lot to grumble about) I almost always use mostly-reliable packages rather than writing my own.
problem: Relies on packages he considers only 'mostly reliable'
need: Publish validation of results against reference datasets so users can trust them

quote: Whenever I learn about a new statistical method: Do I know what I'm doing? - Highly debatable Do I hope for the best? - 100%
problem: Runs new methods without confidence they are applied correctly
need: Guided analyses with assumption checks and a plain-language explanation of what was run

workflow: choosing an analysis in a lab
quote: we didn't use this statistical analysis because no one in the lab knows how to work it and I can't learn it fast enough
problem: The right analysis was skipped because nobody in the lab could run it
need: Guided, step-by-step versions of less common analyses so a lab can run them without a resident expert

quote: Experimental folks in the biological sciences really need to learn how to fill out an Excel sheet. The sheet starts in row 1, column A. ... Plus, you can't keep changing the nomenclature.
problem: Wet-lab spreadsheets are messy and inconsistently named, which breaks downstream analysis
need: Structured data entry with fixed columns and controlled sample names that exports tidy data

quote: We had some code for image randomisation which ran very slowly in ImageJ. Pro: easy to use by labbies Con: very slow, like really slowww
problem: Lab-friendly ImageJ tools are very slow
need: Keep tools easy for bench users while making them fast enough for large image sets

quote: I promised myself a while back that I wouldn't write any more #ImageJ Macro code. ... And here I am again in ijm hell!
problem: The lab still depends on many ImageJ macros that need constant tweaking
need: Reusable, parameterised analysis templates instead of one-off macro scripts

role: Research scientist and lab manager, cell biology PhD (bio)
workflow: adding scale bars to microscopy images
quote: I took images with the same magnification and zoom. I rotated and cropped them in FIJI and added scale bars. The scale bar on one of the images is longer than the others. What is going on. I am literally about to lose it.
problem: Image scale is silently lost after rotate/crop, so scale bars come out wrong
need: Keep calibration through every transform and warn when it is lost or differs between images in one figure

role: Senior Lecturer in Imaging & Calcified Tissues (bio)
quote: Fighting #ImageJ today. It's losing greyscale calibration when I crop a section from a larger image.
problem: Greyscale calibration is lost when an image is cropped
need: Carry intensity calibration with the data through crops and exports

quote: Image analysts: What is your go to method for batch converting image files from the proprietary format to a tiff file?
problem: Proprietary microscope files have to be converted one by one before analysis
need: Batch-import vendor instrument formats directly

role: Runs a spatial proteomics facility, University of Oxford (bio)
quote: However standard ImageJ (bioformats) file handling doesn’t cope well with such large files.
problem: Standard tools choke on 2-4 GB images
need: Handle multi-GB inputs (chunked/lazy loading) without crashing

workflow: comparing bacteria in microscopy images, WT vs mutant
quote: This #ImageJ plugin seems perfect for what I want to do, but the documentation on https://microbej.com is not like the interface on my Mac👇, is there a newer manual somewhere?
problem: Plugin documentation does not match the interface on Mac
need: Documentation and tutorials that match the current interface on every OS

quote: is there a way to calculate directionality on TrackMate? Or if not, is there a file that can be used to calculate directionality later on?
problem: Cannot find how to get a directionality metric or the export that would allow computing it
need: Export per-track tables in a documented format ready for downstream statistics

quote: this appears to make a lot of the analyses that our lab has hard-coded into a very nifty interactive web-app!! Really awesome way to make complex #FlowCytometry analysis accessible when built-in tools to #FlowJo don't quite deliver!
problem: FlowJo's built-in tools fall short, so the lab hard-codes its own analyses
need: Interactive downstream analysis of exported cytometry data (frequencies, MFIs, group stats) without coding

quote: If you use Fiji (ImageJ) I made lookup tables (LUTs) using a color blind friendly color set from Okabe & Ito (2002). It provides a few more options for your image stacks beyond the recommended green/magenta combination.
problem: Few colour-blind-safe options beyond green/magenta
need: Ship colour-blind-safe palettes (e.g. Okabe-Ito) as defaults
